0.value:
shadow reads live motion capture from a Shadow suit, for up to four bodies.

shadow_sensor, which reads the raw sensor values of one sensor, has its own help patch. shadow_pose is not a suit node: it builds a 37-row pose from single joints, and is described on the pose help patch.

CONNECTING:
shadow talks to the Shadow application on this machine, port 32076. On a Mac, if Shadow is not running, creating the node launches it, and the node connects once it is up. 'reconnect' drops the connection and makes it again.

WHAT THE SUIT GIVES YOU:
Each body has a quaternions outlet and a positions outlet, each 37 rows, one per joint in the Shadow layout.

The quaternions are the joint ORIENTATIONS - each joint's rotation, w x y z - and they are the real measurement: the suit is a set of inertial sensors, and orientation is what they produce. The positions are worked out by Shadow from those orientations plus its limb lengths, so they are a derived quantity and only as good as the assumptions behind them. They arrive in centimetres and the node divides by 100, so they go out in metres.

That distinction matters constantly. An orientation error is a sensor problem;
a position error may be an orientation error, or a limb length, or the root inference - see the sensor_to_root help patch.

WHEN IT SENDS:
Frames are read on a background thread. Normally the newest frame goes out once per frame of the app, positions first, then quaternions, body by body; frames that arrive in between are replaced by the newest. With 'direct_out' on, every frame goes out from the background thread the moment it arrives.

SYNTAX:
shadow

EXAMPLE:
shadow

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

flush:
Discard whatever is queued in the connection and start from the current frame. Use it when the stream has fallen behind and you would rather lose data than lag.

reconnect:
Close the connection to Shadow and open it again.

direct_out:
Off by default. On, each frame is sent from the background thread as it arrives instead of once per app frame.

OUTPUTS:

body N quaternions:
The joint orientations for that body, 37 rows of w x y z - the measurement.

body N positions:
The 37 joint positions in metres, worked out from the orientations.

A NOTE ON MULTIPLE BODIES:
The four bodies are separate suits, and the outlets are static - body 3's outlets exist whether or not a third suit is connected, and simply stay quiet. So a patch built for two performers works unchanged with one.

RELATED:
active_joints reduces the 37 rows to the 20 joints most patches use, as in the example.
shadow_sensor shows what one sensor reads before Shadow combines them. take records the stream and plays it back.
